title: Native-context inputs on negotiated typescript-semantic OpenUniverse (capability token native-context-inputs-v1)
description: NORMATIVE field-level publication for native-evidence section 9.5a (contract successor NSS-F1). Closed JSON-vector forms of deterministic-CBOR wire maps: the native-context inputs carrier, the typescript-semantic OpenUniverse payload that carries it, and the token-gated pre-Analyze input-mismatch payload, all lawful only when native-context-inputs-v1 is in both the Hello and the HelloAck token arrays. In every JSON vector a member named <m>Hex is the lowercase hex of the wire CBOR byte string named <m>; the wire map is the vector with each <m>Hex replaced by <m> = bytes(hex). Inherited OpenUniverse members keep their names, types and laws. The scalar members are restated exactly; the inherited universe is named by selector (provider-startup TypeScriptSemanticUniverseV2) and is not restated, so admitting TypeScriptOpenUniverseV3 also requires admitting its universe under that selector, as FA-2 names inherited nested records. Cross-record joins a schema cannot express (the three digest joins, canonical-form re-encoding, the selection rule, the recomputation order and the correlation of the mismatch payload) are stated in x-opensip-native-context-inputs-law.

x-opensip-native-context-inputs-law.standing: NORMATIVE field-level restatement of native-evidence section 9.5a (contract successor NSS-F1). Section 9.5a is the prose owner; where they differ, that is a defect in whichever moved.
x-opensip-native-context-inputs-law.negotiation: Capability token native-context-inputs-v1 (native-evidence 9.1; typescript-semantic only). When it is in both the Hello and the HelloAck token arrays the OpenUniverse payload is TypeScriptOpenUniverseV3, and the pre-Analyze Unavailable payload is PreAnalyzeUnavailableV1 or TypeScriptPreAnalyzeInputMismatchV1. When it is absent the OpenUniverse payload is provider-startup TypeScriptOpenUniverseV2 and the pre-Analyze Unavailable payload is PreAnalyzeUnavailableV1, unchanged. TypeScriptOpenUniverseV3 or TypeScriptPreAnalyzeInputMismatchV1 without the token, or TypeScriptOpenUniverseV2 with it, is PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION. Frame names, phases, transition rows, terminals, limits, commitments, identity tokens, identity versions and protocol major 2 are unchanged.
x-opensip-native-context-inputs-law.planNeed: native-context-inputs-v1 is not an identity token and does not enlarge the identity token set. It is a token the Plan needs (native-evidence 9.1, step 1) for every typescript-semantic worker: a signed row without it is never spawned, and the affected Coverage keys are unknown / provider-unavailable with cause capability-missing.
x-opensip-native-context-inputs-law.carrier: NativeContextInputsV1 {context, configGraph, nodeModulesLayout, unitRoot}. context is the exact retained C bytes of the TypeScriptNativeContextV2 that universe.resolvedInputs.nativeContextId names; configGraph is the exact retained C bytes of the TypeScriptConfigGraphV1 that universe.resolvedInputs.tsconfigGraphHash names; nodeModulesLayout is the exact retained C bytes of the ResolvedNodeModulesLayoutV1 that the context's nodeModulesLayoutDigest names, or null exactly when that digest is null; unitRoot is the rootPath (InternalUnitRootV1) of the WorkspaceUnitV2 the universe was minted for. No other member, and no closure, compiler, stdlib or toolchain record, is carried.
x-opensip-native-context-inputs-law.digestJoins: Before UniverseAccepted the worker checks: (1) "sha256:" + hex(H("native.context.typescript.v2", context)) equals universe.resolvedInputs.nativeContextId, H being the foundation identity frame over the carried bytes as C(X); (2) hex(SHA-256(configGraph)) equals universe.resolvedInputs.tsconfigGraphHash; (3) nodeModulesLayout is null exactly when the decoded context's nodeModulesLayoutDigest is null, and otherwise hex(SHA-256(nodeModulesLayout)) equals it; (4) universe.resolvedInputs.nodeModulesInReadSet equals (nodeModulesLayout is not null). Each carried byte string must parse as the closed record it names and re-encode under C to the identical bytes, and the decoded context and universe must agree where native-evidence 2.4 makes them overlap. A failure of any check is a malformed or uncorrelated OpenUniverse: the worker sends no UniverseAccepted and exits nonzero, and the host observes a process fault. The host checks the same joins before spawn and refuses a failure as a host invariant.
x-opensip-native-context-inputs-law.selection: The worker takes exactly these values from the carrier as host and Plan authority: configGraph.entryConfigPath; the installPath, realPath, packageName and packageVersion of every nodeModulesLayout row, and the layout's presence; the contentSha256 of a layout row whose manifest (realPath with at most one trailing "/" removed, then "/package.json") is not a sealed VFS file; and unitRoot. unitRoot is used only as the start directory of TSR-1 R-6.1 and R-6.2's ancestor walks; it is never a compiler-host, Program, subject or membership input. The worker never infers a selection from a digest, never enumerates configuration or unit candidates to match a digest, and never copies any other member of the carried context, graph or layout into its recomputation.
x-opensip-native-context-inputs-law.recomputation: After SnapshotAccepted the worker derives, in this order: (1) the configuration graph G' by M3-B item 14a's function from configGraph.entryConfigPath over the sealed VFS (G' is {schemaVersion 1, entryConfigPath null, nodes []} when the entry is null); (2) the context X' from G', the sealed VFS, universe.resolvedInputs.programRootFiles (for the js-synthesized jsx rule only), the selection, and its own installed compiler and stdlib closures, under native-evidence 2.4 and TSR-1. It then decides: a refusal at (1) is TypeScriptPreAnalyzeInputMismatchV1 {input config-graph, outcome refused}; a refusal at (2) is TypeScriptPreAnalyzeInputMismatchV1 {input native-context, outcome refused}; otherwise if H(X') differs from nativeContextId the terminal is PreAnalyzeUnavailableV1 (native-context-mismatch, unchanged); otherwise if C(G') differs from configGraph the terminal is TypeScriptPreAnalyzeInputMismatchV1 {input config-graph, outcome differs}; otherwise NativeContextVerifiedV1. A refusal is only a decision of the closed refusal-key set below; any other inability (resource exhaustion, a defect of the worker's own closure or install, a crash) is a process fault and never this payload.
x-opensip-native-context-inputs-law.layoutRecomputation: X'.nodeModulesLayoutDigest is null when nodeModulesLayout is null, and otherwise hex(SHA-256(C(L'))), where L' is the carried layout with each row's contentSha256 replaced by the sealed VFS digest of its manifest (realPath with at most one trailing "/" removed, then "/package.json") wherever that manifest is a sealed VFS file.
x-opensip-native-context-inputs-law.inputMismatch: TypeScriptPreAnalyzeInputMismatchV1 is lawful only in typescript-semantic phase WAIT_NATIVE_CONTEXT_VERIFIED (row T2-10, unavailablePayload pre-analyze) and only under the token. executionId, snapshotId and planId equal OpenUniverse. For outcome differs, input is config-graph, planBoundDigest equals universe.resolvedInputs.tsconfigGraphHash and recomputedDigest differs from it; outcome differs with input native-context is PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION, because that case is PreAnalyzeUnavailableV1. For outcome refused, refusalKey is a member of the closed refusal-key set. After it: WAIT_ZERO_EXIT, zero-exit, WAIT_EOF, eof, DONE, exactly as PreAnalyzeUnavailableV1. A malformed or uncorrelated payload, equal digests, the forbidden combination, an unlisted refusalKey, the payload without the token or outside its phase is PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION and FAULT.
x-opensip-native-context-inputs-law.hostConversion: Identical to PreAnalyzeUnavailableV1's (provider-startup x-opensip-startup-law preAnalyzeUnavailable hostConversion): only after DONE, stage_authority('unavailable'), one host-minted CoverageResultV3 per requested key with deficiency provider-unavailable and a null cause. No stage id, coverage or digest is taken from the worker; input, outcome, digests and refusalKey are operational evidence only and are never a public DomainDetailCode.
x-opensip-native-context-inputs-law.refusalKeysStanding: The four M3-B item 14a keys (input config-graph only) and the TSR-1 section 7 phase 2, 3, 4-references and 5 keys (input native-context only), without subject. TSR-1 phase 1 keys and native-evidence 2.4 closure keys concern the worker's own install and are process faults. TSR-1 phase 4's literal-root and root-count checks are not evaluated by the worker, because programRootFiles is a Plan-bound universe member it does not re-derive. The pairing is checked by the schema: input config-graph admits only the four item 14a keys, and input native-context admits only the seven TSR-1 keys.
x-opensip-native-context-inputs-law.bounds: Each carried byte string is a C encoding admitted under the foundation 4 MiB descriptor bound (identity-and-evidence section 3; product canonical.rs MAX_BYTES 4194304), so the carrier map is at most 12599362 bytes of deterministic CBOR (three 4194304-byte strings with their heads, a maximal 4096-character InternalUnitRootV1 unitRoot and the member keys), and with its own key it adds at most 12599382 bytes to OpenUniverse. The existing maxFramePayloadBytes 67108864 and the host's exact send-schedule measurement are unchanged and remain the only frame bound; no limit member is added.

ExecutionIdText.description: host-allocated ExecutionId text, exact AttemptRecord value

CanonicalBytesHex.description: Lowercase hex of a wire CBOR byte string holding one complete C encoding (at most 4194304 bytes).

contextHex.description: Wire member context: the retained C bytes of native-evidence.schemas.v2.json#/$defs/TypeScriptNativeContextV2 named by universe.resolvedInputs.nativeContextId.

configGraphHex.description: Wire member configGraph: the retained C bytes of native-evidence.schemas.v2.json#/$defs/TypeScriptConfigGraphV1 named by universe.resolvedInputs.tsconfigGraphHash.

nodeModulesLayoutHex.description: Wire member nodeModulesLayout: the retained C bytes of native-evidence.schemas.v2.json#/$defs/ResolvedNodeModulesLayoutV1 named by the context's nodeModulesLayoutDigest, or null exactly when that digest is null.

unitRoot.description: The rootPath of the WorkspaceUnitV2 the universe was minted for: the empty string for the project root, never ".".

universe.description: provider-startup.schemas.v1.json#/$defs/TypeScriptSemanticUniverseV2, unchanged in members and law, named by selector and not restated here. Admission of TypeScriptOpenUniverseV3 is this record AND that selector's admission of universe (composed admission); this standalone record alone does not admit a payload.

TypeScriptOpenUniverseV3.description: typescript-semantic OpenUniverse when native-context-inputs-v1 is negotiated: TypeScriptOpenUniverseV2 plus nativeContextInputs.

TypeScriptPreAnalyzeInputMismatchV1.description: Pre-Analyze Unavailable payload for a native input the worker's recomputation could not confirm while the context id did not differ (native-evidence 9.5a); only under native-context-inputs-v1, only in the NativeContextVerified interval; carries no requested stage or coverage. A native-context recomputation that completes and differs is PreAnalyzeUnavailableV1, never this payload.
